# Define and implement actual-reuse receipts and explicit revenue allocation records

The site can collect a three-game bag, but selection does not establish source reuse or a royalty arrangement. We need an evidence-backed primitive that records actual contributions and, only after explicit agreement and a verified revenue event, allocates a reproducible amount to the accepted beneficiaries.

Proposed chain: **ReuseReceipt → accepted SplitAgreement → RevenueEvent → CreatorLedgerEntry**. The detailed contract proposal is [docs/planning/revenue-sharing.md](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/feat/plugin-discovery/docs/planning/revenue-sharing.md).

## Scope

- Versioned immutable contracts and lifecycle audit events, with actual-used source/version/scope, target revision, rights/notices and behavior validation evidence.
- Creator/payee identity and authority bindings; explicit acceptance of the same immutable terms by every required party.
- Revenue basis, shares, platform/residual treatment, currencies, rounding, refunds and remix scope recorded as terms; unresolved values block activation.
- Trusted revenue ingestion, integer minor-unit arithmetic, idempotent transactional append-only allocation and reversals.
- Private read views that distinguish reuse recorded, terms unresolved, agreement accepted and allocation recorded. No payment claim.

No default royalty is inferred from a license, repository, dependency, bag membership or code quantity. Rates, eligible revenue, platform share and downstream remix inheritance remain open decisions. Payment collection, payouts, settlement, tax/FX, public provenance and banking data are outside this issue.

## Dependencies and sequence

1. Independently review the proposed contracts; implement schemas and labeled fixtures first.
2. Reuse evidence builds on #13 (handoff/source scope) and #16 (integration validation); protected handoff and agreement acceptance depend on verified identity #27. Verified email alone does not establish creator authority.
3. Implement authorized receipt submission and review, then accepted agreement versions with explicit party authority.
4. Choose and verify a trusted revenue adapter before live event posting; implement ledger/refund invariants and crash-safe idempotency.
5. Add authorized site/MCP read views aligned with #26 and C14; validate the actual three-source demo separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Versioned schemas reject malformed integers and incomplete contracts; semantic validators reject selected-but-unused attribution, unpinned or stale evidence, unresolved required rights and accepted agreements with missing terms/acceptances.
- [ ] A validated receipt traces actual copied/adapted contributions to immutable source and target evidence; neither a bag nor an agent claim can self-certify reuse.
- [ ] All required parties accept one terms digest through authorized accounts with reviewed authority bindings; changes require a new version and acceptance.
- [ ] No allocation posts without a validated, undisputed receipt, accepted applicable agreement and trusted verified event. Missing economic decisions remain visibly unresolved.
- [ ] Same idempotency key/payload replays safely; different payload conflicts; concurrent ingestion posts once with no partial batches.
- [ ] Integer calculations conserve the eligible pool, keep currencies separate, account for explicit residuals and cannot multiply shares through repeated provenance edges.
- [ ] Full reversal exactly negates original entries; cumulative partial refunds cannot over-reverse; out-of-order, excessive and mismatched-currency refunds cannot post prematurely.
- [ ] Corrections/reversals preserve original records and refer to the original agreement/rule version. Private records are tenant-scoped and do not expose target code/paths or private identity evidence.
- [ ] UI/MCP state never describes a recorded allocation as paid or displays fabricated earnings. Fixture events are labeled and isolated from production posting.
- [ ] Distinct author/reviewer evidence records actual data/contracts/tests, changed revision/digests and desktop/mobile captures for UI work; explicit PASS precedes closure.

Current status: proposal only. This issue does not assert that a royalty backend, economic agreement or playable remix already exists. The first ready implementation slice is schema/state validation; live commercial activation remains blocked on the explicit product decisions in the proposal.

**Build sequence:** 12a (before #13) · **Priority:** P0 · **Phase:** Local reuse

**Prerequisites:** [#5](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/5), [#8](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/8)

## Problem and outcome

A visitor should be able to browse, search, compare and try games immediately. Before they obtain code through HeadStart or request a reuse handoff to their coding agent, require a verified email and a valid session. After verification, resume the exact selected bag and intended action so the user does not have to rebuild their selection.

This follows the user's current instruction and supersedes earlier PRD statements allowing anonymous platform code exports where those conflict. It does not introduce a paywall, player accounts or a marketing subscription.

## Priority and dependencies

- Sequence: 12a; priority: P0; phase: Local reuse.
- Depends on: [#5](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/5) (05) and [#8](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/8) (08).
- This issue must pass before dependent implementation exposes platform-controlled code export or reuse handoff without this gate. Independent catalog research and public discovery can continue.
- Verify prerequisite behavior and data contracts independently before dependent implementation. An unrelated pending final mockup selection does not block this functional boundary.

## Scope and boundaries

Keep browse, search, public catalog metadata, external demos and public upstream source links open. Keep a local anonymous collection and editable brief available. Public upstream GitHub/Gitea/GitLab repositories remain publicly accessible under their own access rules; do not imply that HeadStart email verification restricts access to those upstream sources.

Require the server to validate a verified-email identity and live session before HeadStart-controlled code downloads, source-content exports, selected-source packages and reuse handoffs. Apply the same authorization policy to direct API requests, generated download URLs and MCP reuse operations. `search_components` and metadata-only `get_component` remain public; any endpoint that returns actual source content uses the code-access policy regardless of its name. Gate `prepare_handoff` when it creates a reuse/code-access artifact. A local agent's existing editing permissions are not globally controlled by a HeadStart account: editing code already present in the user's workspace remains governed by the user's local authorization.

Implement minimal passwordless verification using one coherent approach: a magic link or email OTP. Provide an adapter for localhost delivery preview so the complete flow can be exercised locally without configuring a hosted email provider or sending live email. Do not create provider accounts, configure domains or initiate live email delivery as part of this backlog-authoring task.

Authentication proves email control only. It does not resolve code/asset rights, grant integration authorization, create royalty agreements or bypass source-scope review gates.

## Implementation requirements

- Enforce the gate in a shared server authorization policy; client UI visibility, user-supplied `verified_email` fields and model assertions are insufficient. Derive verification from trusted server state and check session revocation before protected work or delivery.
- Verification challenges are random, single-use, purpose-bound and short-lived. Store only a secure token verifier/hash, expire challenges, cap attempts and consume them atomically. Bind completion to the intended email/challenge and prevent challenge substitution or replay.
- For OTPs, address their limited entropy with a keyed verifier, strict attempt limits and resend/issue throttles. For links, use a sufficiently unpredictable token and a configured canonical origin. Do not log tokens, codes, authentication URLs or credential-bearing request bodies.
- Use a server-owned or signed allowlist of relative return intents; reject arbitrary schemes, external origins and protocol-relative redirects. Never accept an arbitrary client redirect. Store only the minimal bag reference/revision and intended action needed to resume; retain local selections across the verification journey without leaking the bag or token to third parties.
- Establish sessions using secure, HttpOnly cookies with an explicit SameSite/CSRF policy, bounded lifetime, rotation after verification and logout/revocation. HTTPS is required in hosted environments; any loopback-only development exception must be explicit and fail closed outside localhost.
- Rate-limit challenge creation, resends, verification attempts and protected artifact generation. Responses must avoid exposing whether an email is already registered. Add request size limits and expected error responses without revealing session or verification details.
- For MCP, use a supported client authorization mechanism tied to the same verified server identity and authorization policy. Do not ask the model/user to paste email OTPs, magic links or session cookies into prompts. Keep catalog retrieval distinct from permission for local writes.
- Protected downloads must remain protected after creation: re-check authorization at delivery or use narrowly scoped, short-lived download capabilities issued only after verification. Catalog metadata must not leak unprotected generated code-export URLs.
- Model anonymous, challenge-issued, verification-failed/expired, verified, revoked and unavailable-delivery states explicitly. Verification must survive accidental navigation without losing the selected bag; resume only after success and re-check the bag revision, code rights and target action.
- Collect only the email and minimal account/session records required for access. Show the purpose clearly. No newsletter/marketing consent is implied by verification, and no marketing subscription is created.
- Keep auth UI components and tokens adaptable. Follow the currently selected baseline in `docs/design-direction.md` and issue #26; design the new verification states consistently with that baseline and identify the exact reference/version in review.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An anonymous user can browse, search, open allowed public metadata, launch an external demo, follow public repository links and maintain a local collection without login.
- [ ] Platform-controlled code export/download and reuse handoff requests require verified email on the server, including direct requests that bypass the UI and equivalent MCP operations.
- [ ] A crafted client verification flag, missing session, unverified identity, expired session and revoked session are all rejected before source artifacts are generated or returned.
- [ ] One-time link/OTP verification works end to end through the local delivery-preview adapter; expired, incorrect, exhausted, superseded and reused challenges fail safely, including concurrent replay attempts.
- [ ] Return destinations reject open redirects, challenge/session data stays out of logs, and cookie/CSRF/session rotation settings are tested for the selected implementation.
- [ ] The exact anonymous bag selection and intended action resume after verification, with revision/rights revalidation; cancel/error/retry paths preserve the selection without manufacturing success.
- [ ] Protected artifacts cannot be retrieved through a reusable public link or a metadata endpoint that bypasses the gate.
- [ ] MCP public search/metadata remains available, while reuse handoff requires the verified identity. Account verification does not trigger or authorize local filesystem edits.
- [ ] Rate limits and non-enumerating responses are exercised for sign-in issuance, resends and verification attempts; no live email is required for these tests.
- [ ] A localhost setup command and a documented development-only email preview are provided, with an explicit hosted-delivery adapter seam and no dependency on production provider credentials.
- [ ] Desktop/mobile browser evidence covers entry from a selected bag, challenge entry/sent state, expired/invalid state, successful resumption, logout and keyboard navigation. Reduced viewport behavior, focus and accessible error announcements pass independent critique.
- [ ] Independent coder and critical reviewer evidence identifies the reviewed commit/digest, actual tests and screenshots, findings and fixes. Functional/local criteria may pass against a clearly provisional visual reference and unblock specifically verified prerequisites. Under `docs/design-direction.md` and `docs/development-workflow.md`, pending required final visual acceptance keeps the overall issue open until the user-selected baseline is available and reviewed; desktop/mobile usability screenshots remain mandatory now.

## Verification and coder/reviewer loop

Assign a coder subagent to implement and exercise the server gate and local verification flow, then a different critical reviewer to inspect actual server/client/MCP code, tests and desktop/mobile screenshots. The reviewer must attempt direct API and MCP bypasses, replay/expiry, redirect abuse, anonymous discovery and selected-bag resumption, not approve from the coder's summary. Fix blocking findings and repeat independent review until the issue's acceptance criteria pass. Record the review in `docs/reviews/` with the reviewed revision and explicit PASS or CHANGES REQUESTED. Record functional passes separately when useful. If required final visual acceptance is pending, retain CHANGES REQUESTED/open overall with the exact design-baseline blocker; do not close the issue or imply a provisional screenshot is final visual approval. Follow [design direction](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/design-direction.md) and [development workflow](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/development-workflow.md).

## Deferred

Hosted email-provider setup, production email delivery, passwords, social login, billing, player saves, marketing automation and generalized account management are outside this issue. Implement only the minimal identity, verification and session lifecycle needed for the code-access boundary.

## Source of direction

Current user instruction: simple email/login before platform code-grab/use actions, while browsing/shopping remains open. The preserved public-source-link distinction and local-agent write boundary follow HeadStart's catalog/integration separation. Apply this current instruction over conflicting historical no-auth export guidance; do not silently change public discovery into an account-required experience.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Landing matches C4/C4b's light, color, layered coastal world, clear prompt/CTA, Browse all games and bag. Keep text and controls stable. Preserve a connected reachable bridge/path and smaller companion; do not add island clutter.
- [ ] C2 browsing supports scrollable list, accessible Genre/Style/Runtime dropdowns, search, useful empty/error states and list/grid toggle. C3 provides prominent authentic previews, play/source actions, three selected games, removal and a concise editable remix brief.

- [ ] Automatically log original developers and pieces actually used; distinguish selected-but-unused material. Preserve source notices. Show unresolved royalty terms honestly; no invented rates, amounts or payment/settlement claims.
- [ ] Mobile preserves readable prompt/actions, accessible browsing/bag and touch alternatives. Pause world and reduced-motion start still. Keyboard users can complete the journey without decorative motion.
- [ ] Capture actual desktop and narrow-mobile states and compare them to exact reference digests. Record responsive adaptations, motion budget/fallback and intentional deviations. Do not mark static mockups as implemented motion or video.
- [ ] A coder/author subagent and separate critical reviewer inspect actual code, meaningful behavior checks and screenshots. Fix blocking findings and repeat review until explicit PASS in a durable review record. Only then close implementation criteria.

0–6s arrive; 6–14s browse/play; 14–21s collect three; 21–29s ask Astra; 29–40s compressed real adaptation; 40–53s playable payoff; 53–60s actual-used creator/royalty record. **Prerequisites:** [#9](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/9), [#10](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/10), [#17](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/17), [#22](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/22)

## Problem and outcome

Manual review must establish ground truth before model-generated extraction can be trusted. Evaluate whether bounded AI proposals improve curator productivity without unsupported capability or readiness claims.

## Priority and dependencies

- Sequence: 25; priority: P2; phase: Deferred assisted verification.
- Depends on: [#9](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/9), [#10](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/10), [#17](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/17), [#22](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/issues/22)
- Deferred; does not block localhost development or the first local acceptance gate. Begin only after the prerequisite evidence justifies this work.

## Scope and boundaries

Add opt-in bounded capability proposals on top of static parser facts and a held-out expert-reviewed evaluation. Keep proposals private pending curator review. Hosted target connections, broad automatic extraction, cross-engine adapters and public remix graphs remain separately deferred.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create a held-out set of 30 capabilities over at least six categories, including entangled code, dynamic dependencies, missing assets and mixed rights; exclude it from prompt/rubric tuning.
- [ ] Model output must validate against schema and cite existing pinned source paths/symbols; compare every proposed dependency/export with static evidence.
- [ ] Two independent reviewers assess supported-claim precision, required-dependency recall and false-ready labels; target proposed ≥90%, ≥95% and zero known false integration-tested labels.
- [ ] Version model/prompt/analyzer/harness inputs, resource/token limits and outputs; rejected or failed proposals cannot mutate published listings or execute repository instructions.
- [ ] Compare curator time and cost against the manual baseline and publish an evidence-based keep/change/stop decision with remaining failure cases.

## Validation evidence

Run the held-out evaluation and adversarial instruction/path fixtures. Independent reviewer validates labels, metrics, split integrity and cost evidence; visually inspect any preview assertions against authentic rights-cleared source media.

## Required coder and critical reviewer loop

Follow the [development workflow](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/development-workflow.md) and the issue-specific evidence below.

1. Assign a coder subagent to implement this issue with production-grade error handling, clear interfaces, and focused changes. For research, the author subagent produces the research dataset and evidence instead of unnecessary application code.
2. Assign a separate critical reviewer subagent who did not author the changes. Give the reviewer the issue, exact revision/diff, acceptance checklist, and evidence. The reviewer independently inspects the output and runs relevant checks; author self-review does not satisfy this gate.
3. The reviewer checks primary-source citations, pinned revisions, capability/category claims, actual image identity and display rights, representative demo observations, and every proposed eligible record; unsupported claims remain unresolved.
4. For any UI introduced or changed during this issue, attach desktop and mobile screenshots with viewport/browser, scenario and revision; the reviewer must inspect them and critique visual design, accessibility and interaction states under the [design-direction policy](https://github.com/lucasaerb/headstart/blob/main/docs/design-direction.md). Any styling remains provisional until the user selects a mockup baseline; record pending final visual acceptance explicitly. Otherwise explicitly record screenshots as not applicable and review the relevant data, CLI, protocol or runtime evidence.
5. The coder fixes each blocking finding and reruns affected checks; the same independent reviewer re-reviews the new revision and evidence. Repeat until the reviewer explicitly records PASS with no unresolved blocking acceptance or design findings. Do not weaken criteria merely to obtain approval.
6. Save commands, actual results, evidence paths, reviewer findings, fix references and final verdict in `docs/reviews/assisted-analysis-evaluation/`. A blocked external dependency or unavailable test remains open with its limitation; it is never a simulated success. Close only after the independent PASS.

## Source requirements

- `HeadStart-Starter-Package/Playparts-Technical-PRD-v0.3.md` — AI decomposition; AI assisted extraction and verification; Evaluation set; Roadmap dependencies and open decisions.
- `AGENTS.md` — source truth, trust boundaries, UI evidence and working guidance.

- [ ] Art direction outputs an editable guide for palette, geometry, lighting, materials/textures, animation and 2D/3D/asset workflow with coherent choices, concrete mismatches, reference evidence and labeled subjective judgment.

- [ ] Code review cites source locations, dependency/interface/lifecycle consequences for the selected target and prioritized actionable findings; stars and line count do not substitute for review.

All mockups, including preferred explorations, are provisional until the user explicitly selects an implementation baseline.
